learn.prompt: A 12 V source is across a 4 Ω resistor. Set the current.
learn.hint: Use I = V / R. Divide the voltage by the resistance.

learn.prompt: The resistance is fixed. You double the voltage. What happens to the current?
learn.hint: Current is proportional to voltage when resistance is constant.
learn.explanation: I = V / R. Doubling V while R stays fixed doubles I.

misconceptionMap.b: Current and voltage move together when resistance is fixed, not in opposite directions.
misconceptionMap.c: The resistance is fixed, but the voltage changed, so the current must change.
misconceptionMap.d: Doubling voltage doubles current. It does not square the current.

learn.prompt: A 9 V source drives 0.5 A through a resistor. Enter the resistance in ohms.
learn.hint: Rearrange I = V / R to R = V / I.

check.prompt: A 24 V source is across an 8 Ω resistor. What current flows?

misconceptionMap.a: You divided resistance by voltage. Use I = V / R.
misconceptionMap.c: That is the resistance, not the current.
misconceptionMap.d: You multiplied voltage by resistance. Ohm's law divides them.

check.prompt: A 2 A current flows through 6 Ω. Set the voltage across the resistor.
check.hint: Rearrange I = V / R to V = I R.

takeaway.title: One equation, three rearrangements
takeaway.body: V = I R connects the three quantities. Fix any two and the third is determined: I = V / R, V = I R, R = V / I.
